**4 of your Macs are on a macOS version below 15:** two run macOS 14.5 and two run macOS 13.6. All four are failing the `os_up_to_date` check.

**Evidence**
- **DARFCP0BQM2G**: MacBook Pro on macOS 14.5, used by emp-initech-1000. It fails `os_up_to_date` (medium). [DARFCP0BQM2G/2026-06-12]
- **RLD7WV7J82SH**: Mac mini on macOS 14.5, used by emp-initech-1000. It fails `os_up_to_date` (medium). [RLD7WV7J82SH/2026-06-12]
- **SPKRRDF0L786**: MacBook Air on macOS 13.6, used by emp-initech-1003. It fails `screen_lock` and `os_up_to_date` (both medium). [SPKRRDF0L786/2026-06-12]
- **XZYK11QTPWEC**: MacBook Pro on macOS 13.6, used by emp-initech-1000. It fails `screen_lock` and `os_up_to_date` (both medium). [XZYK11QTPWEC/2026-06-12]
- Two of these Macs have only 2.0% of their disk free, which could block a macOS upgrade: DARFCP0BQM2G (20.5 GB free) and RLD7WV7J82SH (5.1 GB free). [DARFCP0BQM2G/2026-06-12, RLD7WV7J82SH/2026-06-12]

**Caveats**
- I used each device's latest snapshot. "Below 15" means a major version lower than 15, so any 15.x does not count. Windows devices were left out of the comparison.
- The search looked at 7 devices. The results don't say whether that means 7 Macs or 7 devices across the whole fleet, so I can't give you an exact total of Macs.
- You asked for a count, so I haven't proposed any actions. If you want to upgrade these Macs, I'd suggest freeing up disk space on the two nearly full ones first.
